headline: Architecture shapes how we live—buildings are frozen decisions about what matters
universal_truth: Environments shape behavior; the spaces we build become the lives we live
fun_facts: Cathedral ceilings make people think more abstractly; low ceilings promote focused thinking
The design of prisons, hospitals, and schools profoundly affects the people inside them
Ancient architects embedded astronomical alignments into structures—Stonehenge, pyramids, temples
discussion_questions: How do the buildings you inhabit affect how you feel?
What values are built into your home's design?
What would a building designed for human happiness look like?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Buildings aren't just shelter—they're statements. A cathedral's towering space makes you feel small before God. A modern office's open plan says 'collaborate.' Architecture freezes decisions about values into structures we then live inside.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We think we live in buildings, but buildings also shape us. How does architecture actually influence human behavior and experience?

options.text: Spaces affect how we move, interact, feel, and think—we unconsciously adapt to our environments
options.response: Yes. High ceilings promote abstract thinking. Natural light improves mood. Hallway layouts determine who we encounter. We're shaped by spaces we barely notice.

options.text: Buildings provide practical functionality that we adapt to
options.response: Functionality matters, but the effects go much deeper into psychology...

q1.title: Ceiling Effects
q1.script: Studies show high ceilings encourage abstract, creative thinking—you feel freed. Low ceilings promote focused, detailed work—you feel contained. The space above your head changes what happens inside it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Ceiling Effects"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Values in Stone
q2.script: Every building embeds values. Prisons are designed to control. Hospitals are designed to heal. Churches to inspire awe. The priorities of designers become the experiences of inhabitants. Architecture is ethics made physical.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Lasting Influence
q3.script: Buildings outlast their makers—often by centuries. The decisions of architects shape generations who never knew them. When you design a building, you're designing how future strangers will live. That's profound responsibility.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Environments shape behavior. Architecture teaches that the spaces we build become the lives we live. Notice the buildings around you—they're silently influencing everything you do.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 160—160 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore what clothes communicate. Until then, notice how different spaces make you feel different ways.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Space Awareness - Notice Your Environments
growTrack.activity: Move through different spaces today and notice how each affects you. A cramped room versus an open one. Natural light versus artificial. Quiet versus noisy. You're being shaped by architecture constantly. What would you change about the spaces you inhabit?
